what_is_priced_in: Continuation of the hyper-growth story into a premium multiple: the reverse-DCF shows the price already assumes a 51.3% FY2027 revenue beat against management's own guidance, a 22.6% revenue CAGR through FY2034, and a 61.9% terminal EBIT margin. On the surface this looks defensible because Oracle's own-history (5-year band, $151.27) and peer (10-name median, $148.70) multiples land within ~3% of today's $153.94 price — the market is not pricing an obvious statistical extreme on a multiples-only view.
what_market_may_be_missing: The SPECIFIC, quantified size of what the price requires versus what has actually been guided or ever achieved: an 18-point beat of a guide issued three weeks ago, and a terminal margin ~15 points above the best margin any named peer (Microsoft) has ever posted — while Oracle's own audited return on capital has fallen every year for four straight years to a level at or below its own estimated cost of capital, and the balance sheet's real constraint (the ~$70bn FY2027 capex program, not the covenant or maturity wall) breaks at a 2%-20% EBITDA decline that sits inside normal-recession range, not a tail scenario. The multiples-only view that makes the stock look fairly priced does not independently test any of this — it is a relative, not an absolute, read.
evidence_engine_is_different: Three independent, non-circular sources converge on the same caution, none of which required assuming the others: (1) valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md's own solver output (51.3% vs 33.6% guided FY27 growth; 61.9% vs 46.8% best-peer terminal margin; $92.3B EV shortfall even at the model's theoretical reinvestment-free best case); (2) business-model/09_moat.md's independently-computed ROIC trend (12.35%→8.22% over FY22-FY26, now at/below the ~11.2% WACC estimate) — built from segment and unit-economics data, not from the DCF; (3) earnings/03_margin-drivers.md's own finding that FY2027 gross margin is guided by management itself to step down further, a genuine headwind rather than a recovering tailwind. This is falsifiable and dated: the FQ1 FY2027 print (2026-09-04) will show whether growth is converging toward the 51.3%/62% price-implied pace or holding near the guided 27-29% range [decision_record.json edge_proof; forecast FC-ORCL-FQ1FY27-REVENUE-2026Q3].
base_rate_check: The MARKET's implied path fails its own base-rate test on three matched axes: (metric) revenue growth vs revenue growth — the price-implied 22.6% 8-year CAGR sits 7.6 points above the DCF's own conservative base case and far above Oracle's own trailing 4-year revenue CAGR of 12.2%; (level) the implied 14-17% global cloud-infrastructure share by FY2030 is tested against the actual historical pace at which AWS and Azure built their current 21-28% shares (the better part of a decade or more), not against a group-average or unrelated benchmark; (period) the nearest, most decision-relevant comparison — FY2027 growth vs management's just-issued FY2027 guidance — shows the price requires beating a three-week-old guide by 18 points, which has no precedent anywhere in Oracle's disclosed guidance history. The ENGINE's own base case, by contrast, is anchored to consensus/guidance being roughly achieved — it does not require an exceptional forecast, it requires the ordinary case. This is why the burden-of-proof asymmetry (CLAUDE.md §9: no exceptional forecast without exceptional evidence) sits against the priced-in path, not against the engine's caution.
